slot.brief: Given the temperature of a gas, find the average translational kinetic energy per molecule (or total for given moles) using (3/2)kT.

stem: The root-mean-square (rms) speed of oxygen ($\text{O}_2$) molecules at a certain temperature is $400\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The rms speed of hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$) molecules at the same temperature is:
notes: from question bank g5308764b24c5 (verified in job 20261126-121821-a29c)
working:
The root-mean-square speed of an ideal gas is given by:
$$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$$

At a constant temperature $T$, the rms speed is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass:
$$v_{\text{rms}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$$

Taking the ratio for hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$, $M = 2\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$) and oxygen ($\text{O}_2$, $M = 32\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$):
$$\dfrac{v_{\text{rms}}(\text{H}_2)}{v_{\text{rms}}(\text{O}_2)} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_{\text{O}_2}}{M_{\text{H}_2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{32}{2}} = \sqrt{16} = 4$$

$$v_{\text{rms}}(\text{H}_2) = 4 \times v_{\text{rms}}(\text{O}_2) = 4 \times 400\ \text{m s}^{-1} = 1600\ \text{m s}^{-1}$$

Independent check: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M), so at the same T, v_H2/v_O2 = sqrt(M_O2/M_H2) = sqrt(32/2) = 4. Hence v_H2 = 4 × 400 = 1600 m/s.
